quotes.text: The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.
Stripe handles the display of eligible payment methods using [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md).
We’ll send you an email confirmation no later than 5 days after your confirmation of this Direct Debit Authority.
If successful, Stripe returns a SetupIntent object with the status `succeeded`. The attached PaymentMethod is now ready to be used for future payments.

findings: The November 7, 2026 full guide explains saving NZ BECS debit details before amount/date are determined (new lines 5–13), with setup distinct from a later debit. May 3, 2026 already has the same purpose and Accounts v2 recommendation/GA-versus-preview qualification (old lines 8–20), but its executable example creates a Customer and explicitly selects `nz_bank_account` (old lines 35–65, 258–275). The current summary lines 13–35 reflects this older Customers v1 path.

Server prerequisites and identities: have a Stripe account, enable NZ bank account in the Dashboard for the documented dynamic flow, and associate the local customer with the ID of a customer-configured Account or a Customer. November uses `configuration.customer: {}` for Accounts v2, a `/v2/core/accounts` creation example with `2026-10-28.preview`, or `/v1/customers`. The `/v1/setup_intents` and `/v1/payment_intents` examples use `customer_account` versus `customer` respectively with `automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true` (new lines 15–19, 33–100 and 267–297). The preview header is shown on Account creation, and participants need an API preview version under the documented condition, without assuming the identical header is demonstrated for every v1 request or that any user has access.

Both captures hand the SetupIntent client secret to the client via an SPA endpoint or server-rendered page. The Payment Element collects name, email, account number and DDA acceptance. Without it, the merchant separately displays the terms and confirms acceptance; mandate records must be provided promptly if Stripe requests them (old lines 68–73, 102–118 and 139–212; new lines 102–151 and 153–224). New lines 233–259 show client `stripe.confirmSetup` with `redirect: 'if_required'` for the nonredirect NZ BECS path, a return URL for added redirect-based methods, errors or `requires_payment_method` versus `succeeded`. Setup success attaches a reusable PaymentMethod; a separate confirmed NZD off-session PaymentIntent attempts the later debit (new lines 267–297). It does not prove settlement, availability of funds, or a paid debit.

Both captures require mandate-and-bank-details email after successful setup and an email giving the amount/date for every debit no later than the day of the debit; Stripe sends by default, with a custom option (old lines 250–256, new lines 261–265). The mandate block changes from 5 business days to 5 days as documented below. Sandbox rows are unchanged in substance: success, insufficient funds and refer-to-customer leave mandate active; no account or debit not authorized make it inactive; one fixture remains processing (old lines 278–308, new lines 299–329). The captured guide ends after the rows, so their pointer to a transition API request ‘below’ is not a demonstrated endpoint.

Concept route: wiki/index.md line 7 to wiki/stripe-index.md lines 259–262 and 742, to wiki/concepts/stripe-nz-becs-debit.md lines 22–36 and 70–85. The acceptance/source and concept routes should distinguish this SetupIntent flow from immediate-payment and migrated mandate flows, and distinguish mandatory send-by debit day from Stripe default send-on-confirmation behavior.
substantive_changes: Adds a concrete Accounts v2 customer-configured Account route alongside Customers v1 for saving and reusing a bank account. May already recommended Accounts v2 and stated GA for Connect and public preview for others, but the access text was incomplete and the flows shown were Customers v1 only. November adds Dashboard **Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts** preview opt-in and shows `configuration.customer`, `/v2/core/accounts`, and example version `2026-10-28.preview` (old lines 8–14, 35–65 and 258–275; new lines 33–100 and 267–297). Documentation expansion does not establish an exact product rollout date.

The November guide directs Dashboard activation and eligible dynamic payment methods and uses `automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true` for SetupIntent and future PaymentIntent in both customer branches. May instead explicitly lists `nz_bank_account` in its `customer` examples. This is a meaningful integration choice shown by the guide, with no evidence that manual enumeration is deprecated or that dynamic display guarantees eligibility (old lines 51–65 and 258–275; new lines 78–100 and 267–297).

The sample Direct Debit Authority’s mandate confirmation promise changes from ‘5 business days’ to ‘5 days’ (old line 210, new line 222). The separate mandate/debit email obligations and Stripe default/custom mechanism remain semantically aligned (old lines 250–256, new lines 261–265). The date-specific statement describes what the captured samples say; it is not independent legal interpretation.

source_assessments.reason: A reader looking for the customer identifier when saving and charging against an Accounts v2 customer-configured Account would copy v1 Customer fields from this entry. A reader using the state line to record setup or send a mandate email might trigger the action after a failed confirmation. The current summary offers neither the November evidence nor a locator explaining the scoped deadline discrepancies.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/set-up-payment, the November 7, 2026 guide documents saving a reusable NZ BECS Direct Debit PaymentMethod before charging. Use a Stripe account, enable NZ bank account in the Dashboard for eligible dynamic payment methods, and create a server-side SetupIntent with `automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true`. Associate either a customer-configured Accounts v2 Account using `customer_account` or a Customers v1 Customer using `customer`, and retain the identity in the later server-side PaymentIntent. The Account flow uses `configuration.customer: {}` and shows `2026-10-28.preview` on Account creation; the guide calls Accounts v2 generally available for Connect and a versioned public preview for other users (new raw lines 33-100 and new raw lines 267-297). With the SetupIntent client secret, the client Payment Element collects name, email, bank account number and DDA acceptance. Without it the merchant displays the terms and confirms acceptance separately. The guide requires mandate records promptly on Stripe’s request. `stripe.confirmSetup` with `redirect: 'if_required'` can omit a return URL for this nonredirect method, but added redirect methods need one. It can error, require a different payment method, or succeed; success attaches the saved PaymentMethod. A separate confirmed off-session NZD PaymentIntent attempts a debit. Neither setup success nor request acceptance establishes its final outcome (new raw lines 102-151, new raw lines 203-259 and new raw lines 267-329). The mandate email follows successful setup, and the date/amount email is due no later than each debit day; Stripe sends them by default with a custom option (new raw lines 261-265). The May capture recommended Accounts v2, but illustrated a v1 Customer and explicit `nz_bank_account`; `source-stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment.md` lines 13-35 preserves the May path and needs both November routes and conditional setup outcomes (old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 35-65, old raw lines 221-256 and old raw lines 258-275).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/set-up-payment, the concrete Accounts v2 customer route, conditional Dashboard opt-in through Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts and the versioned Account creation example, and switch from manually listing `nz_bank_account` to Dashboard-activated eligible dynamic methods are substantive documentation changes (old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 51-65, new raw lines 33-100 and new raw lines 267-297). Keep the May 3 Customer/manual route and old example versions dated in `source-stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment.md`; the November 7 Ruby/ERB and cURL examples, Endive replacing Dahlia, and image/table formatting changes do not establish Node.js, manual-listing or earlier SDK deprecation, and unchanged sandbox cases do not prove live payment success (old raw lines 139-150, old raw lines 278-308, new raw lines 153-164 and new raw lines 299-329). In reciprocal NZ BECS references mark the May integration sample’s 5 business days versus the November sample’s 5 days, consistent with the separate method overview that already said 5 days in May. Both setup captures distinguish this mandate email from the debit date and amount notice due no later than the day of each debit, with Stripe default sending and a custom option (old raw lines 195-212, old raw lines 250-256, new raw lines 207-224 and new raw lines 261-265). Identify the SetupIntent client secret and successful saving separately from the later PaymentIntent and mandate state; neither a successful setup nor a `processing` debit establishes collection or funds availability.
